answer: Shared timing clustering audit logs each identity’s action timestamps and runs pairwise cross-correlation after the epoch. Accounts whose burst intervals align above threshold are grouped; their rewards are frozen pending independent activity. An attacker must give every sybil a decorrelated schedule, so each extra identity pays ongoing jitter management and lost cluster rewards. A garden of dormant accounts still fails the test, and a river of synchronized claims is easy to spot. One voyage through several epochs cannot hide repeated timing echoes.
